original_test_intent: Verify that the successfully retrieved Redfish service-root representation for the intended BMC contains no project-forbidden `Wistron` branding in the approved data scope, with complete evidence that absence is not an artifact of failed, truncated or lossy retrieval.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC firmware, Redfish service root and branding policy; define whether scope is raw JSON body bytes, decoded JSON keys/values, HTTP headers, URI strings and/or recursively linked resources; authenticate through trusted TLS; GET exactly `/redfish/v1`; save status/headers and complete raw body separately; require success/content type and duplicate-aware valid JSON; recursively enumerate the approved in-body paths and scan Unicode/case-normalized content for the exact forbidden token; preserve each match with JSON path/byte context or produce a scan manifest proving coverage; do not mutate OEM metadata.
manual_activity: Engineering supplies the exact branding scan scope, Unicode/case normalization and permitted exceptions; retrieval and exhaustive in-scope scan are fully automatable.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT firmware and exact Redfish service-root endpoint/profile
Policy scope: response body only versus headers, keys, values, URIs, OEM metadata and whether linked resources are included
Case/Unicode/escaping/encoding normalization and exact forbidden token/variants
Permitted exceptions, evidence redaction, trusted TLS certificate/CA and protected authentication
safety_requirements: Verify endpoint and certificate before sending credentials
Require successful HTTP and complete valid JSON before any absence result
Keep errors separate from body and preserve raw body/hash so a parser cannot hide text
Scan exactly the approved scope; do not recursively crawl links by assumption or omit keys/URIs when policy includes them
Issue only GET and stop on wrong target, truncation, parse/encoding ambiguity or undefined exception

Validate transport/content/JSON and enumerate every approved in-scope path/value
Perform deterministic case/Unicode-normalized scan and report exact match contexts
Do not weaken TLS, echo a pass on error, change branding/OEM metadata, guess linked scope or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve normalization, token variants and legitimate exceptions
Approve redaction while preserving search coverage

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: GET `/redfish/v1` is correct and read-only, but `curl ... 2>&1 | grep ... || echo` mixes errors with data, discards full evidence and returns the same message for no match or failed retrieval.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a TLS-validated secret-safe client to save full status/headers/body, require successful valid JSON, then scan raw body and/or structured keys/values/URIs exactly as the approved policy specifies, returning match paths/context.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Exact service-root GET, case-insensitive Wistron absence requirement, readable/correct response and 5/5-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a manifest of raw artifact hash and every structured field searched under a versioned normalization policy, making negative evidence reproducible and independent of shell-pipeline exit quirks.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds secure transport, retrieval validity, complete artifacts, explicit search domain, Unicode normalization, path-level reporting and fail-closed errors.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A grep with no output cannot distinguish clean data from an empty body, authentication page, network failure or binary/escaped representation; scanning only displayed values can miss keys or URIs.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The phrase 'all data' may mean only the service-root body or the entire linked Redfish tree, which changes scope dramatically and must not be inferred; redaction can also remove the forbidden string unless scanning precedes it.

project_override_considerations: If policy truly covers the entire Redfish graph, engineering must provide traversal depth, collections, pagination, cycle handling and exclusions as a separate bounded crawl contract. The literal Procedure fetches only `/redfish/v1`, so recursive expansion is not silently added here.
expected_evidence: BMC/firmware, endpoint/profile and approved scan policy
TLS/client metadata plus complete secret-redacted HTTP status/headers and raw body/hash
Search manifest listing raw/structured domains, paths/counts and normalization/version
Zero-match result or every match with JSON path/raw context and exception disposition
No-write audit, retrieval/scan errors and engineer verdict

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read-only service-root scan is clear. Scope/normalization are supplyable policy inputs, so the case remains fully automatable.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2253 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00035-V001: approve BMC/firmware and exact policy scope for 'all data'—raw `/redfish/v1` body, response headers, JSON keys/values, URIs/OEM fields and whether linked resources are included; define case/Unicode/escaping normalization, forbidden `Wistron` variants and permitted exceptions; approve TLS/authentication, pre-redaction scanning and auditable negative-evidence manifest.

review_improvement: Preserves the forbidden-branding check while converting an error-prone grep pipeline into complete, deterministic and auditable negative evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A negative string assertion is only as strong as evidence that every intended byte/field was retrieved and searched. Shell pipelines often treat a curl error or authentication failure as simply no grep match, and JSON escaping/case/Unicode can hide a literal substring. A validated raw artifact plus a structured path manifest makes absence reproducible. The operation is entirely read-only, but the policy must define whether 'all data' stops at service root or follows links so coverage is neither silently narrowed nor expanded.
